claim: Malaria is caused by infection of the erythrocytes by the parasites Plasmodium.
source: Malaria is caused by infection of the erythrocytes by the parasites Plasmodium.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about malaria etiology.

claim: Inside the erythrocytes, the parasites multiply via schizogony, an unconventional cell division mode.
source: Inside the erythrocytes, the parasites multiply via schizogony, an unconventional cell division mode.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Plasmodium replication.

claim: The inner membrane complex (IMC) is an organelle located beneath the parasite plasma membrane.
source: The inner membrane complex (IMC), an organelle located beneath the parasite plasma membrane, serving as the platform for protein anchorage, is essential for schizogony.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IMC structure.

claim: The IMC serves as the platform for protein anchorage.
source: The inner membrane complex (IMC), an organelle located beneath the parasite plasma membrane, serving as the platform for protein anchorage, is essential for schizogony.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IMC function.

claim: The IMC is essential for schizogony.
source: The inner membrane complex (IMC), an organelle located beneath the parasite plasma membrane, serving as the platform for protein anchorage, is essential for schizogony.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IMC function.

claim: The complete repertoire of IMC proteins and their localization determinants remain unclear.
source: So far, the complete repertoire of IMC proteins and their localization determinants remain unclear.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: TurboID-based proximity labeling was used to compile the proteome of the schizont IMC of the rodent malaria parasite Plasmodium yoelii.
source: Here we used biotin ligase (TurboID)-based proximity labeling to compile the proteome of the schizont IMC of the rodent malaria parasite Plasmodium yoelii.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: In total, 300 TurboID-interacting proteins were identified.
source: In total, 300 TurboID-interacting proteins were identified.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: 18 of 21 selected candidates were confirmed to localize in the IMC.
source: 18 of 21 selected candidates were confirmed to localize in the IMC, indicating good reliability.
evidence: This is a validation result from immunofluorescence assays.

claim: The validation of 18 of 21 candidates indicates good reliability of the proteome.
source: 18 of 21 selected candidates were confirmed to localize in the IMC, indicating good reliability.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the validation data.

claim: 83 proteins of the P. yoelii IMC proteome are potentially palmitoylated based on the existing palmitome of Plasmodium falciparum.
source: In light of the existing palmitome of Plasmodium falciparum, 83 proteins of the P. yoelii IMC proteome are potentially palmitoylated.
evidence: This is based on cross-referencing with published P. falciparum palmitome data.

claim: DHHC2 was identified as the major resident palmitoyl-acyl-transferase of the IMC.
source: We further identified DHHC2 as the major resident palmitoyl-acyl-transferase of the IMC.
evidence: This is a primary finding from localization and expression studies.

claim: Depletion of DHHC2 led to defective schizont segmentation.
source: Depletion of DHHC2 led to defective schizont segmentation and growth arrest both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from auxin-induced degradation experiments.

claim: Depletion of DHHC2 led to growth arrest both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Depletion of DHHC2 led to defective schizont segmentation and growth arrest both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding from auxin-induced degradation experiments.

claim: DHHC2 palmitoylates CDPK1 for its IMC localization.
source: DHHC2 was found to palmitoylate two critical IMC proteins CDPK1 and GAP45 for their IMC localization.
evidence: This is a primary finding from Acyl-RAC assays and localization studies.

claim: DHHC2 palmitoylates GAP45 for its IMC localization.
source: DHHC2 was found to palmitoylate two critical IMC proteins CDPK1 and GAP45 for their IMC localization.
evidence: This is a primary finding from Acyl-RAC assays and localization studies.

claim: Malaria affects more than 200 million people.
source: Malaria, a human scourge caused by the protozoans of the genus Plasmodium, affects more than 200 million people and is responsible for approximately half a million deaths in 2019 (World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from the World Health Organization 2019 report.

claim: Malaria is responsible for approximately half a million deaths in 2019.
source: Malaria, a human scourge caused by the protozoans of the genus Plasmodium, affects more than 200 million people and is responsible for approximately half a million deaths in 2019 (World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from the World Health Organization 2019 report.

claim: The symptoms of malaria are caused by the intraerythrocytic proliferation of the parasites.
source: The symptoms of malaria are caused by the intraerythrocytic proliferation of the parasites.
evidence: This is established knowledge about malaria pathogenesis.

claim: After erythrocyte invasion, the parasites replicate via schizogony to produce up to 32 invasive daughter cells called the merozoites.
source: After erythrocyte invasion, the parasites replicate via schizogony to produce up to 32 invasive daughter cells called the merozoites.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Plasmodium replication.

claim: The IMC is present in the invasive or motile stages such as the merozoites, ookinetes, and sporozoites of all Plasmodium.
source: In Plasmodium, the IMC is present in the invasive or motile stages such as the merozoites, ookinetes, and sporozoites of all Plasmodium, as well as in the male gametocytes of human pathogen P. falciparum (Morrissette and Sibley, 2002; Kono et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC distribution.

claim: The IMC is present in the male gametocytes of human pathogen P. falciparum.
source: In Plasmodium, the IMC is present in the invasive or motile stages such as the merozoites, ookinetes, and sporozoites of all Plasmodium, as well as in the male gametocytes of human pathogen P. falciparum (Morrissette and Sibley, 2002; Kono et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC distribution.

claim: The biogenesis of the IMC begins at the early schizont stage after organelle duplication in the cytoplasm and several rounds of genome replication within the intact nucleus.
source: In the asexual cycle of the Plasmodium, the biogenesis of the IMC begins at the early schizont stage after organelle duplication in the cytoplasm and several rounds of genome replication within the intact nucleus (Matthews et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC biogenesis.

claim: Allocation and packaging of nuclei and organelles into daughter cells are achieved by cytokinesis, in which the PM and the extending IMC coordinately invaginate and surround each daughter haploid merozoite.
source: Allocation and packaging of nuclei and organelles into daughter cells are achieved by cytokinesis, in which the PM and the extending IMC coordinately invaginate and surround each daughter haploid merozoite (Ferreira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on cytokinesis.

claim: The pellicle of merozoite is composed of a single membrane of PM, closely aligned double membranes of the IMC, and 2–3 subpellicular microtubules (SPMT) associated with the IMC.
source: As a result, the pellicle of merozoite is composed of a single membrane of PM, closely aligned double membranes of the IMC, and 2–3 subpellicular microtubules (SPMT) associated with the IMC (Kono et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on merozoite structure.

claim: After invasion into a new erythrocyte, the IMC dissembles at the early ring stage.
source: After invasion into a new erythrocyte, the IMC dissembles at the early ring stage (Ferreira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC dynamics.

claim: The IMC is best recognized as the platform for attaching the actomyosin motor complex-glideosome responsible for parasite invasion and motility.
source: The IMC is best recognized as the platform for attaching the actomyosin motor complex-glideosome (occupying the space between PM and IMC) responsible for parasite invasion and motility (Harding and Frischknecht, 2020; Frénal and Soldati-Favre, 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC function.

claim: The IMC serves to maintain the cell shape and rigidity of the merozoite.
source: It also serves to maintain the cell shape and rigidity of the merozoite (Frénal et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC function.

claim: The cytoplasmic side of IMC is associated with a rigid meshwork composed of several families of proteins, including alveolins.
source: The cytoplasmic side of IMC is associated with a rigid meshwork composed of several families of proteins, including alveolins (Gould et al., 2008), which is important for IMC-SPMT interconnection.
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC structure.

claim: The alveolin meshwork is important for IMC-SPMT interconnection.
source: The cytoplasmic side of IMC is associated with a rigid meshwork composed of several families of proteins, including alveolins (Gould et al., 2008), which is important for IMC-SPMT interconnection.
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC structure.

claim: Systematic proteomic analyses on the IMC protein composition have not been reported due to the difficulty in separating the IMC from other membranes, such as the PM.
source: However, systematic proteomic analyses on the IMC protein composition have not been reported due to the difficulty in separating the IMC from other membranes, such as the PM.
evidence: This identifies a technical challenge in the field.

claim: Known IMC proteins include GAP45, GAP40, GAP50, MTIP, MyoA, ECL1, GAPM1, GAPM2, GAPM3, ISP1, ISP3, and the alveolin proteins IMCp, IMC1c, IMC1e, IMC1f, and IMC1g.
source: Known IMC proteins include glideosome-associated protein 45 (GAP45) (Perrin et al., 2018), GAP40 (Frénal et al., 2010), GAP50 (Bosch et al., 2012), myosin A tail domain interacting protein (MTIP) (Bergman et al., 2003), MyoA (Bergman et al., 2003), ECL1 (Green et al., 2017), GAP with multiple-membrane spans 1 (GAPM1), GAPM2, GAPM3 (Bullen et al., 2009), ISP1, and ISP3 (Wang et al., 2020) as well as the alveolin proteins IMCp, IMC1c, IMC1e, IMC1f, and IMC1g (Kono et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a compilation of previously identified IMC proteins with citations.

claim: CDPK1 and PhIL1 were reported to reside in the IMC of schizonts.
source: In addition, calcium-dependent kinase 1 (CDPK1) and photosensitized INA-labeled protein 1 (PhIL1) were also reported to reside in the IMC of schizonts (Kumar et al., 2017; Saini et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC proteins.

claim: BCP1, MORN1, and CINCH are components of the basal complex, a subcompartment of the IMC at the posterior extending edge.
source: BCP1, MORN1, and CINCH, components of the basal complex, a subcompartment of the IMC at the posterior extending edge, were also recently identified (Morano and Dvorin, 2021).
evidence: This is cited from a recent study on basal complex components.

claim: Most of the known IMC proteins were refractory to gene deletion, suggesting an essential function in the development of asexual blood stage.
source: Remarkably, most of the known IMC proteins were refractory to gene deletion, suggesting an essential function in the development of asexual blood stage (Ferreira et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC protein essentiality.

claim: CDPK1 plays a key role in early schizont development as its depletion or inhibition causes parasite arrest at the early schizonts.
source: CDPK1 plays a key role in early schizont development as its depletion or inhibition causes parasite arrest at the early schizonts (; Kumar et al., 2017; Azevedo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on CDPK1 function.

claim: GAP45 is essential for merozoite invasion.
source: On the other hand, GAP45 is essential for merozoite invasion (Perrin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from a previous study on GAP45 function.

claim: BioID is an engineered bacterial biotin ligase adapted for proximity-based biotinylation of proteins in living cells.
source: BioID is an engineered bacterial biotin ligase adapted for proximity-based biotinylation of proteins in living cells (Roux et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from the original BioID publication.

claim: BioID has been used to identify the protein components of complexes and organelles in different model organisms.
source: BioID has been used to identify the protein components of complexes and organelles in different model organisms (Qin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from a review on BioID applications.

claim: BioID-based proximity labeling has generated organelle- and vesicle-specific proteins or proteomes in Plasmodium.
source: In Plasmodium, BioID-based PL has also generated organelle- and vesicle-specific proteins or proteomes, including those of the gametocyte-specific osmiophilic bodies of P. berghei, the blood stage parasitophorous vacuolar membrane of P. berghei and P. falciparum, the apicoplast of P. falciparum, and the IMC and apical annuli proteins of P. falciparum (Geiger et al., 2020; Boucher et al., 2018; Schnider et al., 2018; Khosh-Naucke et al., 2018; Kehrer et al., 2016; Wichers et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from multiple previous studies using BioID in Plasmodium.

claim: BioID requires parasite exposure to biotin over a long period (18–24 hr).
source: However, BioID requires parasite exposure to biotin over a long period (18–24 hr), which is not ideal or feasible for certain developmental stages with a short life span.
evidence: This is established knowledge about BioID limitations.

claim: BioID does not work well at temperatures below 37°C.
source: In addition, BioID does not work well at temperatures below 37°C (May et al., 2020; Bosch et al., 2021), rendering its application to the mosquito stages of Plasmodium unsuitable.
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on BioID temperature sensitivity.

claim: TurboID was developed by directed evolution.
source: Recently, a new biotin ligase, TurboID, was developed by directed evolution (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the original TurboID publication.

claim: TurboID is faster than BioID.
source: Compared to BioID, TurboID is faster and can work under a broader range of temperatures (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the original TurboID publication.

claim: TurboID can work under a broader range of temperatures than BioID.
source: Compared to BioID, TurboID is faster and can work under a broader range of temperatures (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the original TurboID publication.

claim: The application of TurboID in the Plasmodium has not been reported prior to this study.
source: So far, the application of TurboID in the Plasmodium has not been reported.
evidence: This identifies a novelty of the current study.

claim: TurboID was fused with the N-terminal 20 residues of ISP1 to achieve IMC targeting.
source: IMC targeting was achieved by fusing TurboID with the N-terminal 20 residues of ISP1, a known IMC resident protein.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for IMC-specific proximity labeling.

claim: ISP1 is a known IMC resident protein.
source: IMC targeting was achieved by fusing TurboID with the N-terminal 20 residues of ISP1, a known IMC resident protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ISP1 localization.

claim: 83 of the 300 identified proteins are potentially palmitoylated.
source: A collection of 300 proteins were identified as candidate IMC and IMC-associated proteins, of which 83 are potentially palmitoylated.
evidence: This is based on cross-referencing with published palmitome data.

claim: DHHC2 is a master IMC palmitoyl-acyl-transferase.
source: We further demonstrated DHHC2 as a master IMC palmitoyl-acyl-transferase which plays a critical role in schizont segmentation and merozoite invasion by regulating the IMC localization of CDPK1 and GAP45 via palmitoylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from localization, expression, and functional studies.

claim: DHHC2 plays a critical role in schizont segmentation.
source: We further demonstrated DHHC2 as a master IMC palmitoyl-acyl-transferase which plays a critical role in schizont segmentation and merozoite invasion by regulating the IMC localization of CDPK1 and GAP45 via palmitoylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from auxin-induced degradation experiments.

claim: DHHC2 plays a critical role in merozoite invasion.
source: We further demonstrated DHHC2 as a master IMC palmitoyl-acyl-transferase which plays a critical role in schizont segmentation and merozoite invasion by regulating the IMC localization of CDPK1 and GAP45 via palmitoylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from merozoite invasion assays.

claim: DHHC2 regulates the IMC localization of CDPK1 and GAP45 via palmitoylation.
source: We further demonstrated DHHC2 as a master IMC palmitoyl-acyl-transferase which plays a critical role in schizont segmentation and merozoite invasion by regulating the IMC localization of CDPK1 and GAP45 via palmitoylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from Acyl-RAC assays and localization studies.

claim: TurboID detected robust protein biotinylation in parasites as early as 0.25 hr after biotin incubation.
source: Immunoblot using streptavidin-HRP detected robust protein biotinylation in the cell extracts of TurboID-parasites as early as 0.25 hr after biotin incubation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Protein biotinylation in BioID-parasites appeared at a low level at 3 hr and reached a high level at 18 hr.
source: In contrast, protein biotinylation in the BioID-parasites appeared at a low level at 3 hr and reached a high level at 18 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Both BioID and TurboID had similar labeling activity at 30 and 37°C.
source: Biotin-incubated parasites stained with fluorescently conjugated streptavidin revealed that both ligases had similar labeling activity at 30 and 37°C (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Only TurboID retained its activity at 22°C.
source: Notably, only TurboID retained its activity at 22°C (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: TurboID enabled cytosolic and nuclear protein biotinylation in ookinetes at 22°C when exogenous biotin was added.
source: Costaining with the fluorescently conjugated streptavidin and anti-HA antibody detected cytosolic and nuclear protein biotinylation only in the TurboID-ookinetes when exogenous biotin was added (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: TurboID allows more robust proximity labeling of proteins in living parasites with a shorter biotin incubation time compared to BioID.
source: Compared with BioID, TurboID allowed more robust PL of proteins in the living parasites with a shorter biotin incubation time and is less temperature sensitive.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparative experimental data.

claim: TurboID is less temperature sensitive than BioID.
source: Compared with BioID, TurboID allowed more robust PL of proteins in the living parasites with a shorter biotin incubation time and is less temperature sensitive.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparative experimental data.

claim: The Tb-IMC ligase dominantly colocalized with the IMC protein GAP45 in the IMC.
source: As expected, the Tb-IMC ligase dominantly colocalized with the IMC protein GAP45 in the IMC (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Increased biotinylation was detected in cell extracts in the presence of biotin from the Tb-IMC and Tb-cyto schizonts but not from the EV group.
source: Both immunoblot and dot blot assays using streptavidin-HRP detected increased biotinylation in cell extracts in the presence of biotin from the Tb-IMC and Tb-cyto schizonts but not from the EV group (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot and dot blot data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Biotinylated proteins displayed an IMC distribution in Tb-IMC schizonts.
source: Furthermore, parasites stained with fluorescent-conjugated streptavidin (SA-488) and anti-HA antibody exhibited an IMC distribution (surrounding daughter merozoites) of biotinylated proteins, which colocalized with ligase in Tb-IMC schizonts.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Biotinylated proteins displayed cytosolic and nuclear distribution in Tb-cyto schizonts.
source: The biotinylated proteins and the ligase displayed cytosolic and nuclear distribution in the Tb-cyto schizonts, while scarce signal was detected in the EV schizonts (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The Tb-IMC enables the proximity labeling of IMC in the living schizonts.
source: Therefore, the Tb-IMC enables the PL of IMC in the living schizonts.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization and biotinylation data.

claim: 488 biotinylated proteins were significantly enriched in Tb-IMC compared to Tb-cyto control among three replicates with an adjusted p-value<0.05.
source: 488 biotinylated proteins that were at least two times more abundant in Tb-IMC than that in Tb-cyto control among three replicates and with an adjusted p-value<0.05, were significantly enriched.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: After filtering out 188 proteins not showing transcription peak at schizont, 300 candidate proteins were identified.
source: After filtering out 188 proteins not showing transcription peak at schizont, we narrowed the candidates to 300 proteins (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2H, Supplementary file 1, and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on comparative transcription profiling analysis shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2H.

claim: The 300 Tb-IMC proximal interactors included many known IMC or IMC-associated proteins.
source: These 300 Tb-IMC proximal interactors included many known IMC or IMC-associated proteins, including GAP40, GAP45, GAP50, MTIP, MyoA, ELC, GAPM1, GAPM2, GAPM3, IMCp, IMC1c, IMC1e, IMC1f, IMC1g, ISP3, BCP1, MORN1, CINCH, CDPK1, PhIL1, DHHC1, and DHHC2 (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is supported by the protein interaction network shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: The homologs of the identified proteins have displayed an IMC or IMC-like localization in the Plasmodium, or have been shown to interact or associate with IMC protein baits using immunoprecipitation assay in previous studies.
source: The homologs of these proteins have displayed an IMC or IMC-like localization in the Plasmodium, or have been shown to interact or associate with IMC protein baits using immunoprecipitation assay in previous studies (Bullen et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2017; Hodson et al., 2015; Dearnley et al., 2012; Parkyn Schneider et al., 2017; Yeoman et al., 2011; Vaid et al., 2008;).
evidence: This is cited from multiple previous studies on IMC proteins.

claim: The enrichment of IMC and IMC-associated proteins in the list of 300 Tb-IMC interacting proteins suggests reliable data quality generated by TurboID and quantitative MS.
source: Therefore, the IMC and IMC-associated proteins were enriched in the list of 300 Tb-IMC interacting proteins, suggesting reliable data quality generated by TurboID and quantitative MS.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the presence of known IMC proteins in the dataset.

claim: The Tb-IMC proximal interactors were significantly enriched for interactions using STRING database.
source: To further gain functional insights into the 300 Tb-IMC interacting proteins, we cross-referenced these proteins with other Plasmodium datasets. First, the Tb-IMC proximal interactors were significantly enriched for interactions using Search Tool for Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING) (Szklarczyk et al., 2019), a database of known and predicted physical and functional protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is based on STRING database analysis.

claim: The 300 proteins were segregated into two distinct subgroups (I and II).
source: Notably, these proteins were segregated into two distinct subgroups (I and II) (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is supported by the protein interaction network shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Subgroup I contained 152 proteins.
source: The subgroup I contained 152 proteins while the subgroup II contained 148 proteins.
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the protein interaction network.

claim: Subgroup II contained 148 proteins.
source: The subgroup I contained 152 proteins while the subgroup II contained 148 proteins.
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the protein interaction network.

claim: Most of known IMC or IMC-associated proteins were clustered into subgroup I.
source: Most of known IMC or IMC-associated proteins were clustered into the subgroup I.
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis of the protein interaction network.

claim: Many annotated ER/Golgi secretory- or vesicle trafficking-related proteins were clustered into subgroup II.
source: In contrast, many annotated ER/Golgi secretory- or vesicle trafficking-related proteins were clustered into the subgroup II (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is based on the clustering analysis and GO annotation.

claim: Subgroup II was highly enriched with GO terms including vesicle-mediated transport, vesicle fusion, ER to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport, and Golgi vesicle transport.
source: Interestingly, the subgroup II was highly enriched with the GO terms, including the vesicle-mediated transport (40 proteins), vesicle fusion (11 proteins), ER to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport (13 proteins), Golgi vesicle transport (20 proteins) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, biological process panel), and SNARE complex (14 proteins), endosome membrane (9 proteins), late endosome (7 proteins), and endocytic vesicle (16 proteins) (cellular component panel)
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Subgroup I was mainly assigned with GO terms like the inner membrane pellicle complex, protein lipidation, and palmitoyltransferase activity.
source: while the subgroup I was mainly assigned with the GO terms, like the inner membrane pellicle complex (22 proteins) (cellular component panel), protein lipidation (10 proteins) (biological process panel), and palmitoyltransferase activity (6 proteins) (molecular function panel).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The IMC arises de novo from ER/Golgi-derived material via vesicular trafficking and membrane fusion in the schizonts of each replication cycle of the parasite.
source: The IMC arises de novo from ER/Golgi-derived material via vesicular trafficking and membrane fusion in the schizonts of each replication cycle of the parasite (Gordon et al., 2008; Yeoman et al., 2011; Pieperhoff et al., 2013; Bannister et al., 2000).
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC biogenesis.

claim: Detection of subgroup II enriched with vesicular trafficking and membrane fusion effectors agrees with the notion of the ER/Golgi-derived IMC biogenesis.
source: Detection of the subgroup II enriched with vesicular trafficking and membrane fusion effectors agrees with the notion of the ER/Golgi-derived IMC biogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the data to established knowledge.

claim: Subgroup I and II within the Tb-IMC interacting proteins may reflect the tight and dynamic association between IMC organelle and endomembrane system in schizont development.
source: In addition, subgroup I and II within the Tb-IMC interacting proteins may reflect the tight and dynamic association between IMC organelle and endomembrane system in schizont development.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: 21 candidates were selected among the 300 Tb-IMC interacting proteins for subcellular localization analysis.
source: To assess whether the identified proteins are indeed localized in the IMC, 21 candidates were selected among the 300 Tb-IMC interacting proteins for subcellular localization analysis (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the validation approach shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The orthologues of 9 proteins have been experimentally validated to be IMC-residing or association in the schizonts of P. berghei or P. falciparum.
source: Among these proteins, the orthologues of 9 proteins including PY17X_ 0314700 (CDPK1), PY17X_0617900 (CDPK4), PY17X_1440500 (PKAr), PY17X_0839000 (PKAc), PY17X_1420600 (Rab11A), PY17X_1462100 (MTIP), PY17X_0206000 (PhIL1), PY17X_0525300 (GAPM2), and PY17X_1411000 (PIC5) have been experimentally validated to be IMC-residing or association in the schizonts of P. berghei or P. falciparum (Patil et al., 2020; Bullen et al., 2009; Kumar et al., 2017; Saini et al., 2017; Parkyn Schneider et al., 2017; Fang et al., 2018; Green et al., 2006; Wilde et al., 2019)
evidence: This is cited from previous studies on IMC protein localization.

claim: IMC localization or association of 12 candidates has not been well characterized in the Plasmodium.
source: while IMC localization or association of the 12 other candidates (PY17X_0207400, PY17X_0312400, PY17X_0417300, PY17X_0418000, PY17X_0917100, PY17X_1131200, PY17X_1139700, PY17X_1220300, PY17X_1348200, PY17X_1359500, PY17X_1441500, and PY17X_1453100) (Figure 2B) have not been well characterized in the Plasmodium.
evidence: This identifies novel candidates for validation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: IFA showed clear colocalization of the 9 known proteins with the IMC marker GAP45.
source: As expected, immunofluorescence assays (IFA) showed clear colocalization of the 9 known proteins (CDPK1, CDPK4, PKAr, PKAc, Rab11A, MTIP, PhIL1, GAPM2, and PIC5) with the IMC marker GAP45 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: U-ExM detected the IMC localization of CDPK1 in the cdpk1::6 HA schizonts.
source: Additionally, we performed the ultrastructural expansion microscopy (U-ExM) and immune-EM to analyze the localization of CDPK1 in the cdpk1::6 HA schizonts and both methods detected the IMC localization of CDPK1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by U-ExM data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Immune-EM detected the IMC localization of CDPK1 in the cdpk1::6 HA schizonts.
source: Additionally, we performed the ultrastructural expansion microscopy (U-ExM) and immune-EM to analyze the localization of CDPK1 in the cdpk1::6 HA schizonts and both methods detected the IMC localization of CDPK1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immune-EM data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: 9 of the 12 newly characterized candidates displayed the IMC or IMC-like pellicle localization.

claim: The ectopically expressed GAP45 and CDPK1 could be palmitoylated by cotransfected DHHC2-HA in HEK293T cells.
source: To further confirm DHHC2 as the enzyme capable of palmitoylating GAP45 and CDPK1, we transfected constructs encoding HA-tagged human codon optimized DHHC2 (DHHC2-HA), GAP45 and CDPK1 into the human HEK293T cells. Indeed, the ectopically expressed GAP45 and CDPK1 could be palmitoylated by cotransfected DHHC2-HA, while the PAT catalytic-deficient mutant protein DHHC2/C128A-HA failed to palmitoylate GAP45 and CDPK1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by Acyl-RAC data in HEK293T cells shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The PAT catalytic-deficient mutant protein DHHC2/C128A-HA failed to palmitoylate GAP45 and CDPK1 in HEK293T cells.
source: while the PAT catalytic-deficient mutant protein DHHC2/C128A-HA failed to palmitoylate GAP45 and CDPK1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by Acyl-RAC data in HEK293T cells shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The palmitoylation of cotransfected mouse CD36 protein was independent of Plasmodium DHHC2 in HEK293T cells.
source: As a control, the palmitoylation of cotransfected mouse CD36 protein, which was reported to be constitutively palmitoylated in HEK293T (Tao et al., 1996), was independent of Plasmodium DHHC2 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by Acyl-RAC data in HEK293T cells shown in Figure 6F and cited previous report.

claim: The palmitoylation of GAP45 and CDPK1 was significantly reduced in HEK293T culture treated with inhibitor 2-BP.
source: The palmitoylation of GAP45 and CDPK1 was also significantly reduced in HEK293T culture treated with inhibitor 2-BP (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by Acyl-RAC data in HEK293T cells shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The results in human cells replicate the observations of DHHC2 activity in the Plasmodium schizonts and demonstrate the ability of DHHC2 to palmitoylate GAP45 and CDPK1.
source: These results in human cells replicate the observations of DHHC2 activity in the Plasmodium schizonts and demonstrate the ability of DHHC2 to palmitoylate GAP45 and CDPK1.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the HEK293T cell experiments.

claim: Six candidate cysteines (C5, C140, C156, C158, C169, and C172) were predicted for palmitoylation in GAP45 using CSS-Palm software.
source: To identify the residue(s) of palmitoylation in GAP45, we used an online software CSS-Palm (csspalm.biocuckoo.org) for prediction, which generated six candidate cysteines (C5, C140, C156, C158, C169, and C172) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is based on computational prediction shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Only the C140A mutant displayed the IMC localization similar to wildtype GAP45; other mutants (C5A, C156A/C158A, and C169A/C172A) lost the IMC localization.
source: To test them, we initially generated four constructs expressing HA-tagged GAP45, each with a single or double cysteine-to-alanine mutations (C5A, C140A, C156A/C158A, and C169A/C172A) (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B). These constructs were episomally expressed in the schizonts. Only the C140A mutant displayed the IMC localization similar to wildtype (WT) GAP45; other mutants (C5A, C156A/C158A, and C169A/C172A) lost the IMC localization (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Substitution of C156A/C158A or C169A/C172A impaired the IMC localization of GAP45 C-terminal fragment while C140A did not.
source: We also tested the GAP45 C-terminal fragment (30–184 aa) which displayed an IMC localization when fused with a N-terminal GFP (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and B). Substitution of C156A/C158A or C169A/C172A impaired the IMC localization of this fragment while C140A did not (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B), consistent with the localization for HA-tagged GAP45 in Figure 7B.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The cysteines C5, C156 and/or C158, C169 and/or C172 are critical for IMC targeting of GAP45 and might be the residues for modification.
source: These results suggest that these cysteines (C5, C156 and/or C158, C169 and/or C172) are critical for IMC targeting of GAP45 and might be the residues for modification.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data of GAP45 mutants.

claim: The Acyl-RAC assay detected significantly decreased palmitoylation of GAP45 in the C5A, C156A/C158A, and C169A/C172A mutants, but not the C140A mutant.
source: Indeed, the Acyl-RAC assay detected significantly decreased palmitoylation of GAP45 in the C5A, C156A/C158A, and C169A/C172A mutants, but not the C140A mutant.
evidence: This is based on Acyl-RAC data.

claim: For GAP45, there is an association between IMC localization and palmitoylation.
source: Thus, for GAP45, there is an association between IMC localization and palmitoylation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the correlation between localization and palmitoylation of GAP45 mutants.

claim: The degree of palmitoylation was further reduced in the triple cysteine mutants (C5A/C156A/C158A and C5A/C169A/C172A) relative to the single and double mutants.
source: Additionally, the degree of palmitoylation was further reduced in the triple cysteine mutants (C5A/C156A/C158A and C5A/C169A/C172A) relative to the single and double mutants (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by Acyl-RAC data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Two cysteines (C3 and C252) were predicted as the potential residues for palmitoylation in CDPK1.
source: In CDPK1, two cysteines (C3 and C252) were predicted as the potential residues for palmitoylation (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is based on computational prediction shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Only the C3A mutation caused a complete loss in both protein palmitoylation and IMC targeting of CDPK1 in the schizonts while the C252A mutation had no effect.
source: Using the same approach, we found that only the C3A mutation caused a complete loss in both protein palmitoylation and IMC targeting of CDPK1 in the schizonts while the C252A mutation had no effect (Figure 7E–F)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and Acyl-RAC data shown in Figure 7E–F.

claim: C3 is the critical residue for protein palmitoylation and IMC targeting of CDPK1 in schizonts.
source: suggesting C3 as the critical residue for protein palmitoylation and IMC targeting of CDPK1 in schizonts.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CDPK1 mutant data.

claim: The cysteine residues C5, C156, C158, C169, and C172 of GAP45 and C3 of CDPK1 are evolutionarily conserved among different Plasmodium species.
source: Interestingly, the cysteine residues C5, C156, C158, C169, and C172 of GAP45 and C3 of CDPK1 are evolutionarily conserved among different Plasmodium species (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: C5, C156, C158, C169, and C172 of GAP45 and C3 of CDPK1 are residues for palmitoylation which direct IMC targeting of the proteins in schizonts.
source: Together, these results suggest that C5, C156, C158, C169, and C172 of GAP45 and C3 of CDPK1 are residues for palmitoylation which direct IMC targeting of the proteins in schizonts.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the mutational analysis.

claim: After three independent transfections with each of seven Cas9/sgRNA plasmids, no GAP45 C5A mutant parasites were obtained.
source: We attempted to replace the C5 with alanine in the endogenous GAP45 of 17XNL parasite using the CRISPR-Cas9 method. A 742 bp DNA donor template containing the nucleotide substitution was used for homologous replacement. Seven sgRNAs were designed for guiding the Cas9 complex to the target DNA. After three independent transfections with each of these seven Cas9/sgRNA plasmids, we failed to obtain the GAP45 C5A mutant parasites.
evidence: This is based on the results of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing attempts.

claim: A control mutant parasite clone GAP45 C5C was generated with a silent mutation still encoding C5.
source: In contrast, a control mutant parasite clone GAP45 C5C was generated with a silent mutation still encoding C5 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on the results of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Only mutant parasite clones with CDPK1 C3C, but not CDPK1 C3A, were generated.
source: Using the same approach, we attempted to replace the C3 with alanine in the endogenous CDPK1 of 17XNL parasite. Similarly, only mutant parasite clones with CDPK1 C3C, but not CDPK1 C3A, were generated (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is based on the results of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Palmitoylation of C5 in GAP45 and C3 in CDPK1 is essential for protein function and parasite viability in the asexual blood stage development.
source: Together, these results suggest that palmitoylation of C5 in GAP45 and C3 in CDPK1 is essential for protein function and parasite viability in the asexual blood stage development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the inability to generate C5A and C3A mutants.

claim: This is the first application of TurboID-based proximity labeling in the Plasmodium.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first application of TurboID-based PL in the Plasmodium.
evidence: This identifies a novelty of the current study.

source: Among these proteins, 297 have orthologs in P. falciparum (Supplementary file 1), suggesting a conserved protein composition of IMC in the schizonts of rodent and human malaria parasites.

source: Detection of the subgroup II proteins in this study provided another independent evidence supporting the IMC formation from the ER/Golgi-derived secretory system.

source: We previously reported that DHHC2 is critical for parasite development during the zygote-to-ookinete morphogenesis in the mosquito, and DHHC2 palmitoylates ISP1 and ISP3 for their attachment to the IMC to facilitate connection between the IMC and the SPMT (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from a previous study by the authors.
